findings.text: §25 grants `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py`, `reckon/crew/review.py` and a new test, but every mechanism its deliverable names lives elsewhere: the round that resumed the worker in the cited incident is started by `_repair_launch_refusal`/`compose_repair_for_run` in `reckon/crew/recovery_repair_dispatch.py:781` and `:1047`, the quoted advice is rendered at `:551`, and the blocking classification that produced "3 blocking finding(s)" is `_finding_kind` in `reckon/crew/repair.py:198`. The existing promoted-run refusal at `:796-799` does not cover the plan's "head that is already merged" case, because the coordinator merged the reviewed head into main by hand, so the run carries no ledger row and no `promoted_revision`; the gate the plan asks for is a new ancestry check at the round's start site, in a file the node is not granted

findings.reason: a node can satisfy all three cases without implementing either clause, and its gate would still read green, which is exactly the failure the done-when exists to prevent.
findings.text: §25's three cases test a non-blocking-prefixed record, a disposed blocking finding, and an undisposed blocking finding; none tests a head already merged into main and none tests the "reported as unclassified" clause, which are two of the three deliverable requirements

findings.reason: the two clauses cannot both hold, so the worker must choose one and the choice determines whether a silent finding blocks, is skipped, or is surfaced.
findings.text: §25's deliverable is internally contradictory: clause one requires "a `severity` on every finding", while clause two requires that a finding with no severity and no prefix "is reported as unclassified", i.e. carries none; and clause one also reverses a documented existing rule at `reckon/crew/review.py:42-43` ("a finding that states none carries no severity field, because a defaulted severity is a judgement nobody made") without saying which rule now governs

findings.reason: it is a consequence of the write-path defect above and is repaired by the same grant change rather than by a separate edit.
findings.text: the negative control ("treats a missing severity as blocking again") is aimed at `_finding_kind` in `reckon/crew/repair.py:198-217`, which documents treating an undeclared severity as blocking as a deliberate rule, not at anything in the granted write paths
